answer: A proof-of-spacetime protocol curbs Sybil attacks by forcing agents to prove continuous storage of uniquely encoded data, such as field surveys of floral nectar, LIDAR mapping of a rock ledge, or pigment charts of umber clay. An attacker must acquire and power scarce non-volatile storage hardware per identity, making bulk fabrication economically unviable. However, this imposes high plotting latency on honest participants and privileges entities with idle datacenter storage.
